description: A 30x30 solid box with filter: blur(8px), inset 30px from the viewport's own top-left so the blurred edge has room to spread without hitting the canvas boundary. Proves both that the blur spreads past the box's own original edge and that the blur radius's own real-CSS correspondence to a Gaussian standard deviation is right, not just that something got blurry.

florui.css: .box { width: 30px; height: 30px; margin-top: 30px; margin-left: 30px; background-color: #ff0000; filter: blur(8px); }

classification.reason: Measured against a real Chromium capture: ~12% of pixels differ locally (max_error 3 of 255), but CI's own pinned Chromium build disagrees more on the blur's exact gradient shape (~27%, max_error 8) -- the same cross-build variance already documented for box-shadow-blur's own tolerance. Both cases show the diff concentrated in a speckled ring right at the blur's steepest falloff, with the shape's center and its far, fully-faded edge matching exactly -- two independently-implemented Gaussian kernels disagreeing on the transition band, not a wrong radius or a structural mismatch (either of which would show as an offset, a wrong overall size, or a uniform full-field error instead).
